newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS' HAMPTON OUT 2-3 WEEKS AFTER KNEE SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS' HAMPTON OUT 2-3 WEEKS AFTER KNEE SURGERY.

text.p: Rodney Hampton, the New York Giants' all-time leading rusher, underwent arthroscopic surgery Monday to remove torn cartilage from his right knee and was expected to be sidelined two to three weeks.
Hampton will likely miss the Giants' August 31 season opener at Philadelphia but could be ready for the September 7 game at Jacksonville.
Hampton's right knee locked up as he was walking to the field before Saturday night's preseason game against the New York Jets. An MRI taken Sunday revealed torn cartilage in the knee.
Hampton's backup, Tyrone Wheatley, sprained his left knee and ankle last week in a scrimmage and also did not play Saturday.

The injuries to Hampton and Wheatley placed a heavy burden on rookie halfback Tiki Barber, the team's second round draft choice. Barber rushed for 77 yards on 17 carries and caught seven passes for 63 yards in Saturday's 27-17 loss.

The 28-year-old Hampton is the only player in Giants history to compile five consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. He fell shy of making it six last year when he rushed for 827 yards and averaged a career-low 3.3 yards per carry.
Hampton enjoyed his best season in 1995, rushing for 1,182 yards and 10 touchdowns. He has rushed for 6,816 yards in his seven-year career with the Giants.
